plan: In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' actions, since you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid. Bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above value risks losses if you win. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, I'll bid exactly my value of $36 to maximize expected profit.

In this second-price auction format, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win (not my own bid), there's no benefit to shading my bid down - doing so only risks losing auctions I could have profitably won. Bidding above my value risks negative profit. Therefore, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly my true value of $33, ensuring I win whenever profitable and pay a fair price determined by the second-highest bidder.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid), so bidding my true value maximizes expected profit - I never overpay relative to my value, and I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid. There's no benefit to shading my bid in this format. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $31.
